where in the next verse follows πολὺς ὄλβος [great wealth], which is very correctly said, but strangely πολὺς λιμήν [great harbor]: so that the conjecture of Heimsoeth in the Preface to the Bonn Lectures of 1871 p. VII is not improbable, ταὺς πλούτου λιμήν [a great harbor of wealth], which word Hesychius notes: ταΰς: μέγας, πολύς. ταΰσας: μεγαλύνας, πλεονάσας [great: big, much. having made great, having increased]. The same word lies hidden in Plato Theaet. p. 175c. εἰ βασιλεὺς εὐδαίμων κεκτημένος τ᾽ αὐ πολὺ χρυσίον [if a king is happy and has acquired much gold], where since the Clarkianus codex omits πολύ [much], it should be written κεκτημένος ταῦ χρυσίον [having acquired great gold] with Madvig Adversar. vol. 1 p. 101.
